description: The line plot illustrates the perplexity (PPL) evaluation on the validation set of PG-19 as a function of the evaluation context length, with three different retaining ratios (γ=0.25, γ=0.5, γ=0.75) represented by lines of different colors and markers. The x-axis is labeled "Evaluation Context Length" and is on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 2K to 64K. The y-axis is labeled "PPL" and ranges from 7.7 to 8.2. The line for γ=0.25 starts at a PPL of approximately 8.2 at 2K context length and shows a sharp decline to a PPL of around 7.9 at 4K, then a more gradual decline to a PPL of about 7.8 at 8K. It continues to decline slightly, reaching a PPL of around 7.7 at 16K, and remains relatively stable with a slight increase to a PPL of about 7.8 at 32K and 64K. The line for γ=0.5 starts at a PPL of approximately 8.1 at 2K and follows a similar pattern, with a sharp decline to a PPL of around 7.9 at 4K, then a gradual decline to a PPL of about 7.8 at 8K. It continues to decline slightly, reaching a PPL of around 7.7 at 16K, and remains relatively stable with a slight increase to a PPL of about 7.8 at 32K and 64K. The line for γ=0.75 starts at a PPL of approximately 8.1 at 2K and follows a similar pattern, with a sharp decline to a PPL of around 7.9 at 4K, then a gradual decline to a PPL of about 7.8 at 8K. It continues to decline slightly, reaching a PPL of around 7.7 at 16K, and remains relatively stable with a slight increase to a PPL of about 7.8 at 32K and 64K.
